name: Foodberry
old_description: Foodberry is an innovation company that partners with leading brands to create better bite-sized snacks that are delicious, wholesome, and convenient.
about:
Foodberry is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. The company originated from research at Harvard and MIT, where founder David Edwards — a Harvard professor and serial entrepreneur — developed a plant-based coating technology to tackle two food-system problems: making convenient snacks nutritious and cutting plastic waste. The leadership team includes CEO Marty Kolewe (PhD, MIT/Johns Hopkins), board chair Stefan Catsicas (former Nestlé CTO), and operations head Jose Albelo. (No founding year disclosed.)

Foodberry runs a 42,000 sq ft, SQF Level 2–certified facility in Boston offering co-manufacturing, product development, and technology transfer. Its platform transforms foods and beverages — fruit, ice cream, yogurt, smoothies — into bite-sized, edible-coated snacks. The R&D team works with partners from concept to scale-up and can integrate the coating process into existing lines.

The company serves food and beverage brands in categories such as fruit snacks, frozen desserts, dairy, and convenience foods. Named partners include Bel Group (cheese and fruit-snack lines), Van Leeuwen (ice cream bonbons), Gopuff (ice cream bubbles), and Cape Cod Select (frozen smoothie bites).

Foodberry’s mission is to “make the future of snacking as nutritious, delicious and good for the planet as a natural berry.” Its differentiators are a proprietary, no-mess coating that reduces packaging, an end-to-end innovation model covering R&D through full-scale production, and GFSI-recognized food safety certification.

Foodservice Equipment Agents (F.E.A.) was founded in 1996 in Placentia, California, as a manufacturer's representative firm serving the foodservice equipment market across California and Nevada. The company was established to connect commercial kitchen operators with high-quality equipment brands.

In 2016 the firm launched a sister company, F.E.A. Service, which provides delivery, installation, warehousing, and distribution for several manufacturers. The company also operates demonstration kitchens in Southern California, Northern California, and Las Vegas for hands-on equipment evaluation.

By representing manufacturers such as Prática, Hestan, Dry Ager, and Mibrasa, F.E.A. supplies equipment for cooking, refrigeration, food preparation, and specialty applications.

F.E.A. states its mission is to be the food equipment manufacturer representative in its territory, emphasizing excellence, innovation, and partnerships. The company highlights its NATE and EPA Universal certifications, factory-authorized service capability, and local demo kitchens as key differentiators.

name: Forj Medical
old_description: We’re your all-in, hands-on 100% medical focused CDMO partner, whether you need high-volume global manufacturing or custom full system development.
about:
Forj Medical is headquartered in Arden Hills, Minnesota, with additional facilities in St. Paul and Vadnais Heights. The company operates as a contract design and manufacturing organization (CDMO) focused exclusively on medical devices. Founding year and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

Forj Medical provides end-to-end contract design and manufacturing services for medical devices. Its capabilities span precision molding, printed circuit board assembly, automation, cable assembly, cleanroom operations, polymer and metal 3D printing, and supply chain management. The company also offers design and development services including full system development, electromagnetic sensor design, subassembly design, design for manufacturing and automation, prototyping, and process validation. With 450,000 square feet of manufacturing space across six global facilities, Forj assembles over 250 million devices and components annually and has accumulated more than four million hours of medical device engineering experience.

Forj Medical serves medical device original equipment manufacturers ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies. Its customer base includes companies developing fluid and gas management systems, surgical energy devices, optical systems, electromagnetic navigation sensors, stimulation and active wearables, and consumable components. Notable collaborations include work with Conavi Medical on a surgical imaging device and with Vocxi Health to miniaturize a breath-based cancer detection platform.

Forj Medical positions itself as a fully integrated, medical-only CDMO that combines design, manufacturing, and operational support under one roof. The company emphasizes its vertically integrated in-house capabilities, global footprint with U.S. centers of excellence and near-shore/offshore options, and a quality system certified to ISO 13485 with five FDA establishment registrations.

about:
Forum Plastics LLC operates from Watertown, Connecticut, where it was founded in 1992 as GM Tool & Forum Molding Inc. The business was consolidated under the Forum Plastics name in 2009 and became part of the Squadron Capital group of companies in 2016, which reinvests proceeds into technology upgrades.

As a full-service contract manufacturer, Forum provides injection molding, micro molding, insert and over molding, cleanroom assembly in an ISO Class 7 environment, mold design and fabrication, machining, pad printing, laser marking, and rapid prototyping. The company runs a 101-person operation in a facility that added 10,000 square feet in 2015 and relocated to a new building in December 2025, producing 100,000 to 200,000 parts per month.

Forum serves medical device and life science OEMs and startups, as well as industrial and military/defense customers. Its client base ranges from early-stage ventures needing prototype volumes to global original equipment manufacturers requiring full-scale commercialization support.

The company emphasizes an engineering-based, customer-first approach, offering design-for-manufacturability guidance, project management, and quality systems certified to ISO 13485:2016 and ISO 14001:2015, with ITAR registration. Squadron Capital backing enables continuous investment in advanced equipment such as CT scanning, micro molding presses, and additive manufacturing.

about:
Four Engines Apparel operates from a shop at 201B West Boylston Street in West Boylston, Massachusetts. The company was established in 2020 by Dave Keddy, who began the venture as a home-based operation focused on quality decorations and personal customer service. After building a customer base, Keddy moved the business out of his basement into its current dedicated facility.

The shop provides apparel decoration services including embroidery, screen printing, custom patches, and heat transfers. Keddy brings over 17 years of experience in logo merchandising, having started in screen printing in 2012 after working in paper and plastic printing. The operation handles orders across various garment types and materials, producing branded gear for clients ranging from single pieces to larger runs.

Customers include local small businesses, musical acts, sports teams, and event organizers. The company has produced custom hats for a Las Vegas show, embroidered jackets for a soccer season, and show shirts for Expedition Reptile, a performing group that washes garments weekly. Keddy emphasizes serving small companies that larger facilities often turn away due to low minimum quantities.

The business was founded partly to fill a gap for low-quantity orders that larger print shops decline. A longer-term mission aims to partner with a local charity to fund community music programs, reflecting Keddy's background as a musician and the company's name, inspired by a drumming term. The owner cites a personal drive for consistency and attention to detail as core to the work.

The shop produces made-to-order furniture including dining tables, live-edge slab tables, coffee tables, side tables, desks, entryway benches, sideboards, and buffets. It also fabricates wood-and-steel designs with steel bases made in-house, and builds custom religious items such as kneelers, altars, and credence tables. Four Fields serves residential customers across the Twin Cities metro — Minneapolis, St. Paul, and surrounding suburbs — delivering and installing finished pieces directly to homes.

The company emphasizes careful craftsmanship and attention to detail, aiming for pieces that feel built to last generations. It distinguishes itself through in-house steel fabrication, a collaborative design process, and a refinishing service that extends the life of existing furniture.

name: Franklin food equipment
old_description: Factory-trained repair, maintenance, installation, and sales for most major brands of commercial cooking, food processing equipment, and refrigeration equipment.
about:
Founded in 1981 in Van Buren, Arkansas, Franklin Food Equipment has spent over four decades serving commercial kitchens across northwestern Arkansas and eastern Oklahoma. The company began as a service-focused operation, providing factory-trained repair, maintenance, and installation for major brands of commercial cooking, food processing, and refrigeration equipment.

Today, the company offers a full range of services for both hot-side and cold-side equipment. Technicians handle gas and electric ovens, fryers, grills, charbroilers, steam cookers, walk-in coolers and freezers, refrigerated display cases, ice machines, mixers, dough rollers, slicers, meat processing equipment, and dishwashers. In addition to on-site repair, Franklin Food Equipment rebuilds mixers, dough rollers, meat processing equipment, and dish machines, often at a fraction of replacement cost. The company maintains a large inventory of OEM parts and sells new and used equipment from brands such as Hobart, Berkel, Vulcan, and Traulsen, backed by factory-trained installation. Preventative maintenance plans are also available to reduce emergency breakdowns.

The client base spans restaurants, commercial bakeries, food preparation operations, grocery stores, meat processors, schools, medical and nursing facilities, and correctional facilities. Service calls are dispatched within a roughly 200-mile radius of Fort Smith, covering communities including Van Buren, Fort Smith, Russellville, Conway, Waldron, and Mena in Arkansas, as well as Talihina, Wilburton, Stigler, and Poteau in eastern Oklahoma.

Franklin Food Equipment differentiates itself through its factory-trained technicians, extensive parts inventory, and rapid on-site response. The company emphasizes equipment rebuilding as a cost-saving alternative to replacement and offers preventative maintenance programs designed to extend equipment life and minimize downtime during peak hours.

about:
Friesen's Inc was founded in 1939 in Detroit Lakes, Minnesota. The company has been designing and delivering customized engineering solutions for food processors since its inception, building a reputation on innovative equipment solutions for manufacturing and materials handling plant environments.

The company provides custom engineered processing systems, including conveyors, hydraulic power units, control panels, and belting. Its fabrication capabilities were recently expanded with a state-of-the-art fiber laser center with nitrogen generation, satin finish processes, and passivation bays. An in-house team of engineers, programmers, and production professionals handles design, fabrication, parts manufacturing, and service. The UL-listed IP69K-rated panel shop produces custom control systems.

Friesen's serves the food processing, packaging, and manufacturing industries, with additional belting solutions for agriculture, canning, printing, and package handling. Named customers include Kraft Foods, KLN Enterprise, Monogram Food Solutions (Monogram Meats Snacks), Plumrose USA, and Brown Packing. The equipment is designed for hygienic, wash-down environments and meets food safety and employee safety standards.

The company emphasizes in-house engineering as its backbone, with engineers acting as expert system integrators. Differentiators include 24/7/365 nationwide service and support, factory acceptance testing (virtual or in-person), passivation treatment for hygienic delivery, and the ability to design curved incline conveyors. The focus on attention to detail, food safety, functionality, and hygienic design is cited as the foundation of their approach.

old_description: Full Spectrum Solar is a family owned and operated business that has been proudly serving Wisconsin for 20-years. Founded by brothers and UW-Madison Mechanical Engineering alumni, Burke and Mark have always strived to create a company culture that believes that the ethics of good business practice and contributing to the wellness of nature come first. about:
Full Spectrum Solar was founded in August 2002 in Madison, Wisconsin, by brothers Burke and Mark O'Neal, both University of Wisconsin–Madison mechanical engineering alumni. After Burke returned from a lead engineering role at a large California solar firm, the pair set out to build a Wisconsin-based solar contractor grounded in engineering rigor, quality installation, and long-term customer support. The company remains family-owned and operated.

The firm designs and installs solar photovoltaic systems, home battery backup, electric-vehicle charging stations, and heat-pump water heaters, and provides ongoing maintenance, repair, and storm-damage restoration for existing arrays. Its in-house team includes mechanical and electrical engineers, master and journeyman electricians, NABCEP-certified professionals, experienced roofers, and dedicated project managers. Since inception, Full Spectrum Solar has completed more than 1,500 installations totaling over 28 megawatts of capacity across southern Wisconsin, operating from offices in Madison and Waukesha.

Customers range from homeowners and farms to multifamily housing, healthcare facilities, recreation centers, offices, schools, public agencies, and nonprofit organizations. The portfolio includes ground-mounted arrays for agricultural operations, rooftop systems for commercial buildings, and community-scale projects for municipalities and nonprofits throughout the region.

The company distinguishes itself through an education-first approach—no commissioned salespeople—direct pricing, a single accountable project manager for each job, and a post-installation service department that remains available long after commissioning. Its Madison headquarters earned an ENERGY STAR 100/100 rating, and the firm emphasizes transparent communication, practical system recommendations, and standing behind its work for the life of the system.

Furniture Classics operates from a 10,000-square-foot showroom at 433 West 5th Avenue in Anchorage, Alaska. The showroom spans 10,000 square feet and carries pieces in solid walnut, maple, cherry, leather, and velvet. Financing is available with 18 months deferred interest on purchases over $1,500.

The company serves residential customers throughout Alaska, including homeowners in Anchorage, Girdwood, Eagle River, and the Matanuska-Susitna Valley. They also cater to customers looking for custom-made furniture and one-of-a-kind pieces sourced from national markets such as High Point.

Furniture Classics' stated mission is to provide quality American-made furniture to Alaskans at an affordable price without sacrificing comfort or style. The team emphasizes its 35-plus years of industry experience, which allows it to curate durable, high-quality brands and avoid lower-quality imitations. about:
G. B. Woodworking has operated from Boston, Massachusetts since 1982, when founder Gary Barcus turned a lifelong passion for woodworking into a full-time business.

Work begins with a complimentary design consultation, followed by shop fabrication using finishes such as precatalyzed lacquers, waterborne alkyd enamels, conversion varnishes, and catalyzed urethanes. Barcus emphasizes completing the majority of fabrication in the shop to keep on-site installation to one or two days for typical rooms, with larger installations taking up to a week.

Projects are concentrated in the Greater Boston area, including Brookline, Newton, Wellesley, Weston, and Pride’s Crossing. The firm frequently collaborates with interior designers and serves homeowners seeking high-end, fitted woodwork for renovations and new construction.

Barcus founded the business on the principle of client satisfaction above all, stating that he reads both the client and the drawings to anticipate issues before they arise.

old_description: Since 2008, Our Goals Have Been Simple. Provide Quality Renewable Energy Systems That Our Customers Can Rely On.
about:
GAI Energy, based in Flora, Indiana, was founded in 2008 by electrical engineers Chris Rohaly and Neal Rhodes in nearby Kokomo. The company, now led by CEO Cindy Rohaly, CTO Chris Rohaly, and COO Lamar Sledge, began with a mission to deliver high-quality renewable energy systems to the Hoosier state.

The firm operates as an EPC (engineering, procurement, and construction) contractor specializing in turnkey solar photovoltaic and battery storage installations, as well as microgrid systems. Its in-house team handles design, permitting, procurement, construction, and ongoing operations and maintenance. To date, the company has installed more than 14.5 megawatts of capacity across projects ranging from kilowatt-scale to megawatt-scale systems.

GAI Energy serves commercial, industrial, and agricultural customers throughout north-central Indiana, including farmers, business owners, and utility partners. The company references installations in communities such as Lafayette, Plymouth, Valparaiso, and Carmel, and works closely with local permitting jurisdictions and utility companies.

The founders aimed to exceed the state's minimum electrical code requirements; every project is built to the 2020 National Electrical Code and UL safety standards, with a preference for North American-made components. By managing the full project lifecycle without subcontracting, GAI Energy says it eliminates markups and delivers optimized, client-specific designs rather than cookie-cutter solutions.

name: GLW
old_description: Four decades of craftsmanship means that anything you can imagine made out of wood–we can create it. GLW specializes in manufacturing high-end custom wood products for commercial projects requiring consistent quality and engineering support.
about:
GLW, formerly Great Lakes Woodworking, was founded in 1984 in Detroit, Michigan, when carpenters Mike Mancinelli and Paul LaCroix left their separate jobs to start a business together in a garage. Eventual owner Tony Gatliff later joined to help expand the operation. The partners built the company on enduring relationships and a commitment to craftsmanship, keeping production in Detroit as they grew.

The company design-engineers, manufactures, and installs custom fixtures and commercial environments. Its capabilities span woodworking (solid wood and veneer), glass integration with in-house UV welding, metal finishing and plating, acrylic and plexiglass fabrication, stone (marble, quartz, granite) incorporation, plastic laminate pressing, and upholstery and leatherwork. GLW serves retailers, hospitality venues, corporate offices, athletic facilities, and museums nationwide, delivering projects from storefronts and modular display systems to museum display cases.

GLW’s customer base includes prestigious retailers across the country, with projects ranging from retail fixture rollouts and custom entryways to corporate office interiors and locker rooms. The firm emphasizes value engineering and design flexibility, often developing custom tooling and processes for each job to meet precise standards.

The founders’ original vision centered on engineering as a differentiator—Paul LaCroix noted that engineering “was going to set us apart,” while Tony Gatliff cites product quality and owners who deeply care about their work as hallmarks. GLW positions itself as a partner that streamlines manufacturing and installation, offering fixtures engineered for easy setup and creative solutions to complex spatial problems.

GMS Industries was founded in 1989 in El Paso, Texas, as a family-owned packaging manufacturer. The business remains under the ownership of the Glidden family, now led by second-generation brothers Kris Glidden (CEO) and Cory Glidden (COO), who took over from their parents and continue to run day-to-day operations.

The company produces pressure-sensitive labels (including freezer- and cold-chain-rated adhesives in roll and sheet formats with variable data printing), printed instruction sheets, folding cartons, corrugated and laminate shipping boxes, rigid setup boxes, and printed paper bags. Manufacturing takes place across facilities in the United States and Mexico, with in-house graphic design and prepress based in El Paso. The operation also warehouses and distributes standard corrugated boxes alongside custom runs.

GMS serves food and beverage, consumer packaged goods, pharmaceutical and nutraceutical, cosmetics and beauty, home and hardware, and e-commerce and retail brands. A noted long-term client is Kwikset, cited in a CEO Magazine profile as a decades-long supply-chain partner. The firm also holds a GSA Schedule contract (47QSMS26D004X), making it eligible for federal and enterprise set-aside procurement.

The founders' original premise — that a packaging vendor should feel like part of the customer's team rather than a transactional supplier — still guides the company. The Glidden brothers emphasize direct owner involvement, quote-driven pricing instead of catalog rates, and relationships measured in decades; their longest client has been with the company since its 1989 start.

about:
GOEX Apparel operates from Kansas City, Missouri, where it prints and ships finished garments. The company's supply chain spans 2,700 miles: fabrics are produced in South Carolina from U.S. materials, then cut and sewn at its owned factory in Haiti before final decoration in Kansas City. No founding year or founders are disclosed in public materials.

GOEX manufactures custom-printed apparel and wholesale basics, including eco-triblend tees for retail and promotional markets. Its Haiti facility handles cut-and-sew assembly, while the Kansas City warehouse manages printing and fulfillment. The company emphasizes a transparent, Western Hemisphere supply chain and evaluates fabrics annually for sustainability, using OEKO-TEX ECO PASSPORT certified textiles and Fair Trade certified labels.

The company serves organizations seeking branded merchandise—teams, events, musical tours, and retail partners. Named clients include the Minnesota Historical Society, Black Hills Basecamp, Biomes Marine Biology Center, and Koraa. GOEX also opens wholesale accounts for retailers stocking ethically made blanks.

GOEX positions itself as a "People and Planet First" wholesale apparel company, created to counter supply chains that prioritize low cost over people. It pays Haitian workers 65 percent above the sector minimum, holds Fair Trade Federation verification, B Corp certification, and memberships in the Fair Labor Association, Social Enterprise Alliance, and Social Enterprise World Forum. The mission is to create fair-wage jobs that strengthen families and communities.

about:
GT Sales is headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, with its physical location on Parkway Boulevard in West Valley City. The company was founded in 1965 by Gordon Tyler as a manufacturer's representative for both electrical supply and lighting lines. The lighting side of the agency was spun off in the mid-1980s, leaving the firm focused solely on electrical products. In May 1997, Tyler sold the business to Daryl Cook, who had been in electrical distribution since 1975. Cook moved the operation to its current site in early 1999 and purchased the building in 2003, quadrupling the available space from 5,000 to 20,000 square feet.

The firm acts as a manufacturer's representative and stocking distributor for more than a dozen electrical brands, including Arlington Industries, Elite Components, MGM Transformer, RectorSeal, and Voltec. The 20,000-square-foot warehouse is complemented by a fenced 15,000-square-foot yard and a 2,500-square-foot office with a conference room. A team of 11 handles inside and outside sales, logistics, and warehouse operations across the region.

GT Sales serves electrical wholesalers and distributors in the commercial, residential, education, HVAC, utility, and industrial sectors. Its territory covers the Intermountain West: Utah, southern Idaho, eastern Nevada, western Wyoming, and Montana. The company positions itself as the liaison between manufacturers and distributors, helping wholesalers access new products and stay current on technology.

The company's stated mission is to empower progress by connecting customers with the highest-quality electrical solutions, built on lasting partnerships, trust, and innovation. Core values emphasized by leadership include integrity, innovation, partnership, excellence, and commitment.

The company was founded on the premise that analog gaming offers a vital counterpoint to an increasingly screen‑centric world, and its mission centers on restoring human connection through purpose‑built gaming surfaces.

The company manufactures a line of premium gaming tables — including the Origins 2.0, the larger Origins 2.0 Max, and the touch‑enabled Arena Digital Game Table — each configurable with choice of wood tone, rail style, and a proprietary water‑resistant Dynamic Gaming Suede playing surface. Tables are built from solid wood with features such as vaulted recesses for component storage, modular add‑ons (DM Command Centers, cup holders, dining tops), and a lifetime warranty.

Products target the tabletop hobby market: board gamers, tabletop RPG groups, miniature wargamers, and card‑game enthusiasts. The company cites “thousands of families” and “the biggest names in board gaming” as customers, though specific clients are not named. Tables are positioned as home furniture that blends into modern interiors while serving dedicated play.

The founders frame the business as a response to digital isolation, emphasizing accessibility without compromising quality. Differentiators highlighted by the company include the Omotenashi‑inspired service philosophy, consumer‑driven design iteration, freight‑protected shipping, and a lifetime warranty that underscores the expectation of decades‑long use.

Gartland Distributors operates from Biddeford, Maine, where it was founded in 1999 by Bob Gartland. What began as a one‑man venture selling beef jerky from a pickup truck grew into a recognized snack distribution business serving central and southern Maine. In June 2025, ownership passed to Jim and Christine Faiella, experienced small‑business operators who had run community markets in the region for over 15 years. The firm distributes a full line of snack foods — nuts, trail mixes, candy, meat snacks, and a growing selection of better‑for‑you and vending items — with an emphasis on products made in Maine. Its service model includes product rotation, merchandising support, and order management for each account, allowing customers to maintain stocked shelves without handling logistics themselves. Gartland’s customer base spans hospitals, schools, health centers, independent markets, and local shops throughout its service area. The company cites these segments as its primary markets, reflecting a focus on institutional and retail outlets that require reliable, frequent snack replenishment.

The company says its differentiation lies in a “best possible service” philosophy that bundles rotation, merchandising, and ordering with competitive pricing and a 100 % guarantee program. The founders’ original commitment to personal relationships and local sourcing continues to shape the operation under the new ownership.

Gary Weeks and Company Furnituremakers operates from Wimberley, Texas, where it was founded in 1992. The business bears the name of its founder, Gary Weeks, and describes itself as an American company of artisans running a small custom shop.

The facility comprises a woodshop, showroom, finishing rooms, and a lumber shed.

The company sells directly to residential customers worldwide, shipping to every U.S. state and to Europe, Australia, Asia, Africa, and South America. Its customer base is reflected in more than 1,500 published patron reviews and testimonials.

The firm emphasizes a comfort guarantee on its rocker—full refund with round-trip shipping paid by the shop—and broader guarantees of delivery, satisfaction, and service. old_description: General Spring has been America's leading automotive leaf spring and suspension authority since 1965
about:
General Spring of Kansas City, Inc. operates from New Century, Kansas, in the Kansas City metropolitan area. The company was founded in 1965 by Paul Flood, who envisioned a full-service repair shop specializing in automotive leaf springs. After Flood’s brother Jim took over in 1985 and moved operations to Olathe, the business passed to Jim’s son, Jim Jr., and later to Joe Wallace in 2004.

The company manufactures and supplies leaf springs, coil springs, shackles, U-bolts, shocks, and add-a-leaf kits for a wide range of vehicles. It maintains in-house manufacturing and modification capabilities, allowing customization of stock leaf springs to customer specifications, such as replacing stock clips with metal riveted clips for added strength. General Spring also warehouses products at its Kansas City location and ships from multiple distribution points nationwide, visually inspecting each part before dispatch.

General Spring serves both DIY enthusiasts and professional suspension repair shops across the automotive aftermarket. Its product line covers light trucks, heavy-duty trucks, SUVs, and off-road vehicles, with specific applications for brands including Chevrolet, Ford, Jeep, Toyota, and Nissan. The company also supports fleet and commercial customers needing heavy-duty suspension upgrades.

General Spring differentiates itself by working exclusively with manufacturers that are full members of the Spring Research Institute, ensuring high quality-control standards. It offers a one-year warranty on all replacement leaf springs, guarantees products meet or exceed OEM specifications, and provides fast shipping—most stocked items ship within 24 hours. The company emphasizes knowledgeable customer support and the ability to customize springs for unique requirements.

old_description: Gentuity was founded by members of the original LightLab team who helped pioneer the first-generation OCT systems used in cath labs worldwide. about:
Gentuity, LLC is based in Sudbury, Massachusetts. The company was founded by veterans of the original LightLab team that pioneered the first-generation optical coherence tomography (OCT) systems used in catheterization laboratories worldwide. Drawing on decades of experience advancing intravascular imaging, the founders set out to develop a next-generation OCT platform that would overcome the limitations of traditional systems.

The high-frequency OCT technology captures a full-length coronary image in a single one-second pullback, delivering a comprehensive view of the artery. The system is designed for plug-and-play integration into existing cath lab workflows without the need for sterile bags.

The technology targets interventional cardiologists performing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for coronary artery disease. Clinical case studies highlight use at institutions such as Tampa General Hospital and The Christ Hospital. In 2026, Gentuity announced that its advanced intravascular imaging solutions would become available in the United States through a distribution partnership with GE HealthCare.

The company states its mission is to "cross new frontiers in cardiovascular care so patients can focus on living," emphasizing that clearer visualization leads to more informed treatment decisions. Gentuity differentiates itself with the Vis-Rx catheter's ultra-low profile, rapid one-second imaging, and workflow simplicity, aiming to provide confidence at every step of complex PCI procedures.

about:
George C. Moore, a family-owned manufacturer of narrow elastic fabrics and rigid webbing, traces its roots to 1909 when George C. Moore founded the company in Westerly, Rhode Island. The business remains privately held and operates as the parent of two wholly owned divisions: the original George C. Moore Company, focused on stretch and rigid narrow fabrics (woven and knit), and Darlington Fabrics, which produces stretch and rigid wide warp‑knit fabrics.

Today the company runs a U.S. headquarters in Westerly that houses sales, engineering, design, R&D, and technical support, while a 2006 investment created a vertical weaving and knitting facility in American Park Free Zone, El Salvador. That plant produces elastics and webbings from ¼ inch to 12 inches wide and includes in‑house dyeing and finishing, rotary printing, cutting and sewing, performance finishes, and custom packaging. Two dedicated research and development divisions support new product development and custom design for brands.

The company serves a broad range of end markets, including swim, dance, and yoga apparel; underwear waistbands and trims; ballistic protection for military uniforms and law‑enforcement body armor; work apparel and flame‑resistant uniforms; safety and industrial protective equipment; team‑sports gear such as goggles, pads, and helmets; performance compression and activewear; and orthopedic, medical, and stretch‑loop products requiring latex‑free, hook‑receptive surfaces.

George C. Moore emphasizes continual innovation and customer support as its founding premise, citing competitive pricing, consistent quality, and on‑time delivery as reasons it has remained a preferred supplier for over 110 years. Sustainability initiatives have cut heating and cooling energy use by 35%, lighting energy by 40%, and water‑usage ratio by 44%, while recycling programs reuse wooden pallets, cardboard, and plastic bags.

about:
Glaser Steel has operated in Colorado Springs, Colorado, since 1945 when Eugene Glaser and his brother-in-law Frank Holley opened H & G Welding in a former horse stable downtown. The business became Glaser Welding Works under Eugene’s sole ownership, with his wife Darlene handling bookkeeping, and later transitioned to the Glaser Steel name. It remains a family-owned enterprise, now led by the third generation—Jacque Glaser Jensen and her husband Tony Jensen—after successive stewardship by their son Burton “Buddy” Glaser and his wife Charolette.

The company stocks mild steel and aluminum in full lengths or cut-to-size, and maintains a drop pile for remnant pieces. Its shop at 619 South 31st Street, occupied since 1969, provides custom saw cutting, shearing, drilling, punching, welding and fabrication, and CNC plasma cutting of sheet and plate; a 2005 expansion added a plasma table and dedicated sheet storage. The firm also delivers materials and finished fabrications to local job sites.

Glaser Steel serves customers across the Colorado Front Range, supplying raw steel and fabricated components for projects ranging from ornamental railings and window covers to structural fabrications. The business does not list specific industry sectors but works with anyone requiring steel supply or custom metalwork.

The company traces its differentiation to its continuous family ownership and its evolution from a blacksmith shop into a full-line steel supplier and fabricator, a shift accelerated in the 1990s when expanded inventory sparked a surge in retail sales.

Since 1977, duck hunters, sport and commercial fishermen have experienced access to areas that no other marine engine can deliver with total confidence . Confidence that comes from over 35 years of research and testing in hostile conditions such as heavy vegetation, mud trenches, cypress swamp and rock-laden rivers. It’s been called “The Four-Wheel Drive” of marine engines.
about:
Go-Devil Manufacturing-Louisiana was founded in 1977 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. The company began by developing longtail marine engines designed to navigate shallow, vegetation-choked waters where conventional outboards fail.

Today the firm produces a range of shallow-water propulsion systems and vessels, including longtail engines, surface-drive engines, two hull types of aluminum boats (duck-hunting and surface-drive models), floating duck blinds, weedless propellers, and a line of accessories such as fuel tanks, push poles, and the Duck Picker feather-removal device. Nearly all components are fabricated in-house at a facility spanning more than 40,000 square feet, staffed by over 30 full-time employees across sales, marketing, and production.

The primary customers are duck hunters, sport fishermen, and commercial fishermen operating in the swamps, marshes, and rock-laden rivers of North America. The company notes that its engines are in use in every U.S. state and Canadian province.

Go-Devil emphasizes that its differentiation comes from decades of real-world testing in hostile shallow-water environments, which informs every design decision. It also highlights its in-house parts manufacturing and comprehensive replacement-parts inventory as the foundation for responsive customer support.

Gohmann Supply, LLC is a family-owned business founded in 2009 by Chris and Heather Gohmann in St. Cloud, Minnesota. Chris Gohmann brought seven years of hands-on experience from a central Minnesota meat market, where he worked from kill-floor cleanup to retail sales, before joining a national manufacturing firm as a service technician, technical trainer, and regional sales consultant for the Southwest U.S. His enduring passion for meat processing led the couple to establish their own supply company.

The company operates as a distributor of food processing equipment and supplies, offering both new and pre-owned machinery alongside consumable items such as trolleys, gambrels, and rail components. Gohmann Supply represents multiple equipment brands and emphasizes responsive service and technical support, drawing on Chris Gohmann’s background in equipment service and training. The business runs from a facility at 23784 67th Avenue in St. Cloud.

The firm’s mission statement underscores a focus on providing quality equipment and supplies backed by service and support to this sector.

The venture was born from Chris Gohmann’s desire to stay connected to the meat-processing trade after years in corporate roles, aiming to combine better brand selection with personalized service that puts the customer first.

about:
Golden Solar was founded in 2006 in Golden, Colorado, and has remained locally owned since its inception. The company began as a solar installation contractor serving the Denver metro area, focusing on residential and commercial photovoltaic systems.

The firm designs, develops, and installs complete solar PV systems, including solar panels, battery storage (such as Tesla Powerwalls), smart EV chargers, and home automation integration. Its niche is home microgrids, which provide autonomous power during grid outages. The company also offers service and repair for existing installations, and provides financing consultation to help customers access federal tax credits and utility incentives.

Golden Solar serves homeowners, business owners, and non-profit organizations throughout Colorado, with a concentration in the Denver metropolitan area. Its commercial projects are tailored to building size and energy needs, while residential installations include monitoring systems that track performance and yield.

The company’s stated purpose is “empowering people and communities to take control of their energy future” through decentralized energy and microgrid technology. Core values emphasize doing the job right the first time, treating business as a relationship, accountability, teamwork, and attitude as a multiplier.

name: Goose Woodworking, LLC
old_description: *Please note – Goose Woodworking, LLC specializes in making custom, handmade furniture out of high-quality hardwoods and products. As a general rule, we do not build anything out of pine or construction grade lumber from big box stores.
about:
Goose Woodworking, LLC operates from Leesburg, Virginia, where owner and lead craftsman Wayne runs a small business built around custom, handmade furniture. The company's name comes from an old Army nickname of Wayne's, reflecting an 'Army of One' ethos in which the person who designs and builds each piece is the same person who stands behind its quality. A backend team handles operations, but the shop's output remains directly tied to the founder's hands-on involvement.

The shop produces chairs, benches, dining tables, coffee tables, and home decor items exclusively from premium hardwoods such as walnut, sapele, mahogany, cherry, maple, and white oak, milled in-house. Projects begin with client inspiration photos and specifications, move through CAD-generated design drawings for approval, and then proceed to hand construction and finishing. Typical lead times run eight to ten weeks on a first-in, first-out schedule secured by a 50 percent down payment. Finishes range from Rubio Monocoat hard wax oil and Tung oil to custom blends, Arm-R-Seal, conversion varnish, milk paint, and stained topcoats, with stain colors matched using off-cut samples from the actual build.

Clients are primarily homeowners and interior designers seeking pieces that echo styles seen at retailers like Wayfair, West Elm, or Restoration Hardware, or on platforms such as Pinterest and Instagram. The company does not work with pine or construction-grade lumber, positioning its output above mass-produced imports. Each project is a one-off collaboration, with the design phase allowing minor changes at no cost before the signed drawing locks in the build.

The combination of in-house milling, customer-approved CAD drawings, and stain sampling from project-specific off-cuts is intended to eliminate surprises and deliver furniture that matches the client's vision in both material and finish.

Grain Designs operates from Fargo, North Dakota, where it was founded in 2013 by architectural designers who began building furniture in a two‑stall garage. The studio has since grown into a design‑and‑build workshop rooted at The Pines, a creative hub where craftsmanship and community intersect.

The company produces custom hardwood furniture for both commercial and residential clients, including reception desks, office desks, conference tables, live‑edge tables, dining tables, and podcast/media desks. Every piece is fabricated from solid hardwoods, finished to order, and delivered fully assembled; typical turnaround is as little as six weeks from design approval.

Grain Designs serves businesses across sectors such as financial services, media production, and corporate workspace design. Its portfolio includes projects for NorthStar Financial (conference tables, sit‑stand desks, shelving), You Betcha! (office desks, podcast table, container bar), and Enclave Companies’ flagship office (meeting tables, conference table, shelving). The firm reports having helped more than 100 businesses outfit their office spaces.

The founders started Grain Designs to create meaningful, well‑crafted furniture that lasts, rejecting imported mass‑production in favor of North Dakota‑made pieces built on client relationships. The company positions its custom work at or below the price of standard commercial office furniture, emphasizing on‑time, on‑budget delivery and a free design consultation that yields detailed drawings and finish options.

about:
Grand Forks Welding & Machine traces its roots to 1885, when a blacksmith shop called Grand Forks Foundry opened in Dakota Territory to repair riverboats. The business evolved over more than a century into the present-day operation in Grand Forks, North Dakota. No founders are named in the available records, and ownership structure is not disclosed.

The company provides custom fabrication, repair, machining, and drive-line services, supplemented by CNC plasma cutting and custom U-bolt manufacturing. It maintains an in-stock inventory of steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and plastics, and runs a fully stocked parts department supplying brands such as Neapco, Weasler, Waterscheid, and Dexter for driveline, PTO, and trailer components. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not published.

The shop serves builders, manufacturers, and agricultural producers — sectors that have relied on its capabilities since the riverboat era. Concrete examples include fabricating new items, repairing existing designs, and supplying replacement parts to keep equipment running in construction, industrial, and farm settings.

The company emphasizes a reputation for high-quality work and responsive service, noting that its highly trained staff can design, build, or repair almost anything a customer requires. The original mission — keeping river traffic moving — expanded into a broader commitment to minimizing downtime for modern industrial and agricultural clients.

name: Great Plains Energy Corridor
old_description: The Corridor was tasked with providing innovative approaches that bring people together to advance the development of North Dakota's abundant and diverse energy resources.
about:
The Great Plains Energy Corridor was established in 2008 at Bismarck State College in Bismarck, North Dakota, through the initiative of former U.S. Senator Byron Dorgan.

It leverages Bismarck State College's nationally recognized energy education programs, which deliver state-of-the-art training to current and future industry employees. The Corridor's office is housed in the National Energy Center of Excellence (NECE) building on the BSC campus, a facility dedicated in September 2008 that incorporates a ground-source geothermal heat pump system, LEED-compliant lighting, a total energy heat recovery system, and Flexcrete—a construction material made with fly ash from coal combustion.

The Corridor serves partners across government, education, and the private sector, facilitating collaboration to promote energy-related activities through federal funding and other sources. The annual EmPowerND Energy Conference and the North Dakota Energy Report are among its key outreach vehicles, though the 2023 conference was canceled.

The Corridor's distinguishing feature is its integration within a college that operates a LEED-certified, energy-efficient facility purpose-built for energy education, giving it direct access to training infrastructure and a mandate to connect diverse energy stakeholders across the state.

Green Mountain Furniture has operated in Ossipee, New Hampshire, since 1975. Moser Engineering operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in Portland, Indiana. The company was founded in 1986 by Greg Moser, who initially launched the business to support his own drag-racing habit at the Muncie strip. Today it remains family owned and operated.

The shop forges, heat-treats, and machines U.S. steel sourced from domestic mills to produce custom axles, complete rear-end assemblies, differential options, brake packages, and chassis/suspension components. Product lines include the Muscle Pak rear assemblies, circle-track/oval packages, and applications for GM, Ford, and Mopar platforms. Most custom orders ship in two business days or less.

Moser Engineering cites three pillars for its approach: domestic manufacturing with full process control, rapid turnaround enabled by that control, and direct racing experience that informs product development. Staff includes current and former racers and builders, many with decades of tenure.

name: Grillo & Co
old_description: Grillo and Co creates beautiful bespoke furniture for your home or workplace. Operating almost entirely by commission, we custom design and hand make each piece to your exact specifications at our workshop in Golden, Colorado. We will help you visualize your ideas and, once you’re completely happy with the proposed design, we hand-craft your unique heirloom piece of furniture.
about:
Grillo & Co operates a woodworking workshop in Golden, Colorado, where founder John Grillo produces custom furniture on commission. Grillo trained at the Thomas Chippendale International School of Furniture in Scotland, where his work earned the Richard Demarco Prize and recognition in Furniture & Cabinetmaking Magazine and The Scottish Times. A member of the Fine Furniture Guild, he established the studio to blend contemporary and traditional techniques in one-off pieces for homes and workplaces.

The shop designs and hand-builds freestanding furniture including dining tables, writing desks, console tables, side tables, and cabinets. Each project begins with a client consultation and 3D sketches, followed by a 50% deposit and fabrication using joinery such as dovetails, tambour doors, and parquetry. Materials range from domestic hardwoods — walnut, maple, cherry, figured cherry — to exotic veneers like pepperwood and burl walnut.

Grillo & Co serves residential and commercial clients seeking heirloom-quality pieces. Past commissions include a walnut coffee table for a homeowner, multiple pieces for a repeat collector, and unusual custom projects for a client who returned for a second order. The company also offers home and office visits to match existing décor, indicating an interior-design adjacent clientele.

The firm emphasizes award-winning craftsmanship, direct designer-to-client pricing, and freedom from commercial supply-chain delays. Grillo’s Chippendale training and guild membership underpin a design philosophy that treats furniture as functional art, with every detail — down to dovetail style — tailored to the buyer.

about:
Hahn Packaging operates from Fort Smith, Arkansas. Founded in 1923 by sisters Bird Smith Johnson and Isla Re Smith Vaile as the TJ Smith Box Company, the business began in their garage with two pieces of used equipment. The sisters served as the sales force across Arkansas, Oklahoma, Missouri, and Louisiana. Since 1996, the company has been owned and operated by two generations of the Hahn family; Richard Hahn led as president until 2014, when his son Chris Hahn assumed ownership. The firm adopted its current name in 2023 to mark its second century.

The company manufactures paperboard folding cartons and rigid set-up boxes. Folding cartons are produced in styles such as tuck-end, auto-lock, and gable-top, with the option of 100% recycled content. Set-up boxes feature printed exteriors and custom-cut interior trays for product protection and presentation. The operation includes pre-press and print production departments, offering design, prototyping, and full production through shipping. Volumes range from 1,000 pieces to several hundred thousand per order.

Hahn Packaging sells to wholesalers, distributors, and industrial customers across multiple sectors. The company does not disclose specific industry verticals beyond general wholesale and distribution channels.

The founders started the business to supply custom boxes regionally; the Hahn family continued the legacy citing a commitment to quality and innovation. The company emphasizes forward-thinking exploration of new technologies and materials while maintaining heritage standards.

name: Hawaii Technology Development Corporation (HTDC)
old_description: HTDC is a dynamic state agency driving Hawaiʻi’s economic diversification by fostering innovation, developing talent, and providing capital.
about:
Hawaii Technology Development Corporation (HTDC) is a state economic development agency headquartered in Honolulu, Hawaii. Created legislatively in 1983, it operates as an attached agency to the Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism (DBEDT). The corporation was established to develop Hawaii's technology sector and diversify the state's economy.

HTDC does not manufacture products. Instead, it provides a range of services to foster innovation and support businesses across the islands. As Hawaii's Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) center, its INNOVATE Hawaii program enhances productivity and technical performance of small and medium-sized manufacturers. The agency also operates the Hawaii Center for Advanced Transportation Technologies (HCATT), which has over 20 years of hydrogen and fuel cell research in partnership with the U.S. Air Force. HTDC offers co-working space, educational programs, funding opportunities, mentoring, and workforce development initiatives. It reports assisting over 300 companies and helping create more than 3,000 jobs, with $62 million in federal funding secured and $72 million in funding obtained.

HTDC serves technology startups, manufacturers, and energy companies across Hawaii. Its manufacturing assistance reaches small and medium-sized manufacturers statewide. The energy tech program focuses on hydrogen and fuel cell research for national and state needs. The agency also supports aerospace and ocean technology entrepreneurs, as highlighted in recent news about efforts to stem outmigration of young talent. Customers include startups seeking incubation, manufacturers needing technical guidance, and research organizations pursuing clean energy integration.

HTDC was created to address the need for a dedicated state entity to build a sustainable technology and innovation ecosystem. Its differentiating role is as a public-sector catalyst that connects businesses with capital, infrastructure, mentoring, and federal partnerships to accelerate commercialization and job creation in high-value sectors.

References and free estimates are standard practice.

Hinzman Millworks Inc. is a fifth-generation, family-owned hardwood manufacturing company based in West Union, West Virginia. The business has been passed down through five generations of the Hinzman family, building a legacy in Appalachian hardwood processing.

The company specializes in producing premium American white oak staves for bourbon barrels, with expanding capacity for wine barrel staves. Its operations encompass timber procurement, sawmill processing, stave manufacturing, kiln drying, and custom lumber milling. Product lines include barrel staves, dimensional lumber, cants, railroad ties, construction-grade hardwood, and coal mine cribbing. The facility employs sustainable forestry practices and selective harvesting methods to ensure long-term forest health.

Hinzman Millworks serves cooperages, distilleries, wineries, construction firms, mining operations, and infrastructure projects. Its white oak staves are used by major bourbon producers such as Buffalo Trace, and the company has supplied West Virginia Great Barrel Co. International markets include cooperages, flooring manufacturers, and furniture makers in Europe, Asia, and South America, with kiln-dried products prepared to meet export moisture standards.

The company emphasizes craftsmanship, sustainability, and operational efficiency as core differentiators. Direct partnerships with local landowners and loggers secure a consistent supply of tight-grain Appalachian oak while supporting the regional economy. Ongoing investments in kiln drying and export preparation aim to broaden the company's reach in global value-added hardwood markets.

Horizon Nut Company, founded in 2007 in Lost Hills, California, operates as a grower-owned pistachio processing facility. The business is owned by 45 family-farmer members who supply the crop, and it is led by a group of industry pioneers with decades of experience in California pistachio production.

The company provides hulling, drying, and full pistachio processing services for its member growers. It is currently expanding its operations to meet rapidly growing demand, with a stated goal of reaching 100 million pounds of annual processing capacity. The facility handles the entire post-harvest process from farm to table.

Horizon Nut serves pistachio growers throughout California’s Central Valley, which produces 99 percent of the U.S. pistachio crop. Its customer base consists of the 45 grower-owners, who are hands-on farming operations, and the company positions itself as a dedicated partner for moving their crop from harvest to market.

The cooperative model is central to Horizon Nut’s identity: because the growers own the processor, the company says it never compromises on quality and processes pistachios “the way farmers intended them to be.” The structure aligns processing decisions directly with the interests of the farming families who supply the raw product.

Houston Transformer Company, LTD., founded in 1969, operates from a 33,000-square-foot climate-controlled facility in Houston, Texas. The company was established as a manufacturer of custom transformers, inductors, chokes, and related magnetic devices.

The company designs and builds magnetic components ranging from sub-miniature surface-mount devices to three-phase distribution transformers weighing over 1,500 pounds. Its in-house capabilities include custom core configurations (toroidal, bobbin, layer-wound, water-cooled, transposed windings), winding with copper and aluminum conductors, and a full machine shop and sheet-metal department that produce bobbins, cases, NEMA enclosures, and sensor housings. The engineering staff brings over 75 years of combined design experience, and the workforce of 51–200 employees handles prototype through production volumes.

Houston Transformer serves energy exploration and drilling operations, medical and biomedical equipment, military and aerospace programs, audio and lighting/LED manufacturers, data-processing and industrial-process-control systems, and communications OEMs. Products are sold in single-piece quantities as well as to original equipment manufacturers.

The company emphasizes a “can-do” philosophy and unwavering customer focus, citing continuous improvement, cycle-time reduction, and adoption of cutting-edge technology as ongoing goals. Its reputation for dependability in extreme environments—up to 450 °F (250 °C) and 10 kV—stems from rigorous testing, traceability, and compliance with UL and other industry standards.

Howard Industries is a private investment firm based in Ellisville, Mississippi, founded in 1969 by Peter Howard. Howard, who holds an economics degree from Principia College and an MBA from Columbia University, previously worked in strategic consulting at Arthur Young & Company and as a principal at another private investment firm. He established Howard Industries to provide patient capital and long-term support to management teams building market-businesses in manufacturing and specialized services.

The firm deploys its own capital across a portfolio of small and medium-sized manufacturers and business service companies, with investments ranging from $100,000 to $100 million. Howard Industries seeks niche manufacturers and service providers with defensible market positions and compelling customer value propositions.

The firm differentiates itself through its use of proprietary capital, which eliminates external fund pressures and ensures a high certainty of close. Its approach emphasizes candid communication, incremental operational improvement, and alignment with management on long-term strategy rather than short-term exits. Howard Industries remains an active director in all its investments, providing strategic guidance and operational support.

Hybrid Electronics is a family-owned electronic components distributor headquartered in Sanford, Florida. Founded in 2005, the company began as a Florida-based operation focused on helping manufacturers manage excess inventory and source hard-to-find parts. Customers come from commercial, industrial, medical, automotive, and high-reliability sectors, including aerospace, mil-spec, and industrial control markets. The company serves OEMs, EMS providers, and contract manufacturers that need to liquidate surplus stock or procure allocated, obsolete, or end-of-life components.

Hybrid Electronics emphasizes confidentiality, speed, and simplicity: no proprietary portals, no minimum lot sizes, and a straightforward three-step process from spreadsheet to payment. The firm positions itself as a supply-chain partner that turns idle inventory into working capital while protecting customers' bill-of-materials data.

about:
Interconnect Cable Technologies Corporation (ICTC) was founded in 1988 in Brooksville, Florida, where it maintains its corporate headquarters. The company began as a specialist in low-volume, high-mix cable and wire-harness assemblies for original equipment manufacturers worldwide.

Today ICTC operates as a full-service contract manufacturer with facilities in Brooksville and Titusville, Florida, as well as Laguna, Philippines, and Dongguan, China. Its capabilities span cable and wire harness assemblies, printed circuit board assemblies (PCBA), electronic box builds, precision machining, and turnkey assembly services. ICTC serves aerospace, military and defense, industrial machinery, health care, datacom/telecom, and transportation safety sectors. Aerospace customers receive aircraft wiring and harnesses inspected to AS9102 standards; defense programs use Mil-Spec cable assemblies and power-supply system integration; medical devices are built under ISO 13485 requirements; datacom clients get molded networking and power cables; and transportation projects include video security systems for public transit and embedded data collection for roadway infrastructure.

The company emphasizes a hybrid manufacturing model that combines U.S.-based precision and intellectual-property protection with global cost efficiency. Its vertically integrated structure manages circuit card assembly, precision machining, and box build in-house, while global supply chain services provide strategic labor balancing, optimized logistics, Kanban inventory, and tariff navigation. ICTC states its mission is to simplify supply chain and manufacturing challenges and its vision is to be the most trusted, friendly, and flexible contract manufacturer.

Icon Modern was founded in 2007 by Rocky Levy and Aaron Tvrdy in Chicago, Illinois. The founders, who met through a shared passion for sustainable design, started in a garage and quickly secured projects with national brands such as Starbucks, Whole Foods, and Twitter.

The company produces commercial furniture and architectural elements — conference tables, community tables, reception desks, space dividers, ceiling elements, feature walls, planters, and countertops — using a broad range of materials including urban hardwoods, steel, stone, glass, and veneers. Icon Modern imposes no minimum or maximum order quantities and emphasizes shorter lead times through a streamlined process.

The firm serves architects, interior designers, and corporate clients across hospitality, retail, technology, and corporate office sectors. Notable projects include installations for Caterpillar, Jump Trading, and IPG, alongside the earlier brand-name work. A dedicated project manager oversees each job from concept through installation, handling engineering, detailing, and logistics on the client's behalf.

Icon Modern's founding mission centers on sustainability and creative reuse: sourcing all materials within a 100-mile radius of its Chicago shop and giving urban trees a second life as furniture. The team, which includes architects and designers, aims to make custom fabrication more accessible to designers by offering a wider material palette and a collaborative, end-to-end service that eliminates the need for clients to coordinate multiple vendors.

Founded in 1974 in Grangeville, Idaho, Idaho Sewing for Sports began as a small local business sewing truck seats. Co-founders Will and Gail Williams identified a need for quality padding in the ski industry over 40 years ago. The company is woman-owned and operates as an Idaho-based U.S. manufacturer.

The company designs and manufactures custom safety padding for ski areas, gyms, and sports venues across North America. They use heavy-duty UV-resistant vinyl, high-density foam, and closed-cell foam, with capabilities including custom sewing, made-to-order sizing, custom colors and logos, and sustainable recyclable options introduced in 2022.

Idaho Sewing serves ski areas (600+ worldwide), athletic facilities (schools, rec centers, stadiums), playgrounds and parks, adventure parks, climbing gyms, ropes courses, and amusement parks. Customers include ski resorts such as Brooks Lake Lodge and Four Seasons Ski Center, which have used their tubing products since 1995.

The company emphasizes personal customer service, with padding experts guiding clients from quote through design, manufacturing, and delivery. Their differentiation includes nearly 50 years of expertise, all-weather materials, custom-fit solutions, and pioneering the industry's first 100% recyclable padding. They are a member of the National Ski Areas Association.

old_description: Idaho Pacific Holdings, Inc. is a family of potato dehydration companies spanning North America – from the nutrient rich farmlands of Idaho to the San Luis Valley of Colorado to the red sandy soils of Prince Edward Island, Canada.
about:
Idaho Supreme Potatoes operates in Firth, Idaho, where it began as a fresh potato packing operation in 1967. The facility added dehydration capacity in 1969 and grew into one of North America's potato dehydration plants. In 2018, Idaho Pacific Holdings acquired the company and continues its tradition of supplying dehydrated potato products worldwide.

The plant produces dehydrated potato flakes, flour, slices, dices, and shreds/hash browns, with ingredient specifications ranging from whole flake to finely milled flour, full-cook to low-leach, and additive-free clean-label options. Foodservice lines include blended or agglomerated mashed potato mixes, scalloped and au gratin casseroles, and seasoned or unseasoned hash browns. An in-house R&D team develops custom formulations. Packaging runs from poly pouches, gabled cartons, and #10 tins to kraft bags, bulk sacks, and bulk rail or truck loads, with private-label options for foodservice and retail.

The facility sources Russet varieties such as Burbank, Norkotah, and Ranger from Idaho's Snake River Plain.

The operation highlights its diverse production capabilities, custom specification development, private-label packaging, bulk rail and truck logistics, and certifications under a GFSI-benchmarked standard, Kosher (OU), and Halal (IFANCA).

Image Pointe was founded in 1977 in Waterloo, Iowa, to serve unions across America with custom-branded, union-made and USA-made apparel and promotional products. Its in-house art department provides custom graphic design, while production capabilities include screen printing, embroidery, and cut-and-sew manufacturing under the Dignity Apparel label—garments that are "born, built, and sewn in the USA." The combined team numbers over 150 people, with more than 80 at Image Pointe alone; average tenure runs 15 years for union graphic artists and 17 years for screen-printing and embroidery operators.

The customer base consists almost exclusively of labor unions and affiliated organizations. Testimonials on the company's site reference the Columbus Education Association, UAW Local, and IBEW Charlotte, among others, highlighting quick turnaround, design support, and product quality for events, membership drives, and awareness campaigns.

Image Pointe says its difference lies in a mission to create "dignified, life-changing jobs" with fair wages, benefits, and safe conditions. It pledges 100 percent union labor for all graphics and production, guarantees USA-made products (union-made wherever available), and emphasizes rapid turn times and high-impact design as core commitments.

The operation is SQF certified, Organic certified, and RSPO certified, with a full-time maintenance crew supporting continuous distribution.

The business was built on three core commitments: dependable service, quality products, and lasting customer relationships. Those principles, reinforced by family ownership and industry certifications, remain the foundation of its growth strategy today.

about:
Impact Energy & Roofing Denver is based in Centennial, Colorado, and serves communities across the Front Range including Aurora, Denver, Greeley, Lakewood, and Pueblo. The company was established to provide integrated roofing and solar solutions without relying on subcontractors, though a specific founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The firm delivers complete roofing services — repair, replacement, installation, emergency response, and commercial roofing — alongside solar system installation, battery backup, and EV charger installation. All work is performed by an in-house crew that handles both roofing and solar projects back-to-back. The process begins with satellite-based roof and site assessment, followed by shade analysis and Total Solar Resource Fraction calculation, custom design with transparent pricing, and final installation and activation. The company reports more than 3,000 completed projects.

about:
Indiana Rubber & Plastic, LLC has operated from Indianapolis, Indiana since 1936. The company specializes in custom molded plastics and rubber, offering turnkey service from concept through prototype to volume production.

Its capabilities span prototyping via 3D printing, SLA, rapid molding, and silicone molds; rubber molding through compression, transfer, injection, and LSR/LIM processes; plastic injection molding; die cutting; extrusion of both plastics and rubber; lathe-cut rubber; machined plastics; and bonded rubber-to-metal components. The facility handles prototypes of 1–50 pieces, short runs of 1–5,000 pieces, medium runs of 5,000–25,000 pieces, and high-volume orders exceeding 25,000 pieces, with high-tonnage, large-platen presses for oversized parts. On-site tooling and proprietary low-cost Tool$aver® methods support quick-turn tooling.

The company works with a broad material portfolio including silicone, EPDM, Viton, nitrile, neoprene, fluorosilicone, and other rubber compounds, as well as engineering plastics such as PEEK, polycarbonate, nylon, ABS, and thermoplastic elastomers. It produces grommets, gaskets, seals, bumpers, diaphragms, bushings, extrusions, mounts, formed hoses, boots, and washers/spacers for customers requiring food-grade and military-specification materials.

Indiana Rubber & Plastic emphasizes three generations of experience, in-house design, chemistry, and laboratory resources, and a commitment to keeping projects “in network” by leveraging established supplier relationships. The firm highlights communication throughout the supply cycle—from inquiry through tooling, production, and shipment—as a core differentiator.

about:
Industrial Semiconductor, Inc. was founded in 1991 by Fred Marquardt in Granville, Illinois. Marquardt, a former U.S. Air Force technician with experience in vacuum-tube and solid-state electronics, had previously worked on SCR development at National Electronics and served on the JEDEC standards committee. The company incorporated in 2004. In 2015, ownership passed to Steven Malavolti, a 20-year U.S. Navy veteran who had joined the firm in 2007 and rose to general manager.

The company operates as a mainline stocking distributor of high-power semiconductors, including SCRs, diodes, bridge modules, thyristor modules, diode modules, GTOs, and IGBTs. It carries products from manufacturers such as Dynex, Times Electric, RIRI Power Electronics, GE, Westinghouse, Infineon, Powerex, Mitsubishi, Westcode, and IXYS. Industrial Semiconductor also provides heatsink extrusion and assembly services, producing air-cooled thyristor assemblies, diode-heatsink assemblies, and SCR-heatsink assemblies. The firm emphasizes same-day shipping on stocked items with no minimum order requirement and maintains an extensive inventory supported by technical staff rather than traditional sales personnel.

Early in its history, the company developed solid-state timing systems for SCCA and NASCAR racing and portable timing equipment for Ford Motor Company’s road racing team.

The company distinguishes itself by offering only new, factory-tested components that meet original OEM specifications, backed by a team of technical problem solvers. Its model prioritizes direct customer contact over e-commerce automation, aiming to match specific application requirements with the right component and support.

Integra serves neurosurgeons, plastic surgeons, ENT specialists, and wound-care providers. Its products are used in procedures ranging from hydrocephalus management and pediatric ear surgery (AERA® registry) to liver surgery using CUSA® technology. The company partners with physicians to deliver safe, fast, and effective treatments across these specialties.

Integra positions its manufacturing as purpose-driven, emphasizing "Where Manufacturing Meets Purpose." The company highlights its global leadership in neurosurgery, evidence-based regenerative technologies, and long-standing innovation such as 20 years of CUSA® technology as differentiators.

about:
Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions (IMS) was founded in 2005 in Londonderry, New Hampshire, to fill a market gap for high-quality rapid prototype and small-lot printed circuit board assembly. The company was acquired by Perimeter Solutions (NYSE: PRM) on December 24, 2024, broadening its portfolio to include acquisition and sustainment of OEM legacy product lines.

IMS provides full life-cycle electronics assembly services, spanning quick-turn prototypes, high-mix low-volume production, box build, design-for-manufacturability analysis, and end-of-life support including IP acquisition. The New England facility operates multiple SMT lines with Mycronic pick-and-place machines, Heller reflow ovens, 3D AOI and X-ray inspection, selective and wave soldering, and aqueous cleaning. The company emphasizes rapid turnaround, shipping prototypes overnight anywhere in the United States and delivering tested assemblies within hours for short-notice orders.

IMS serves aerospace and defense, medical and instrumentation, communications, consumer electronics and IoT, automotive, and industrial sectors. Reference customers include an automotive technology company, a consumer robotics company, and an IoT solutions provider, all citing the firm's speed, quality, and flexibility in moving from prototype to full box build.

The business was purpose-built to address the lack of responsive service for complex, low-volume PCBA projects. Management, with over 25 years of shared EMS experience, focuses on minimizing time-to-market and mitigating excess and obsolete inventory charges. The Perimeter Solutions acquisition adds a model for acquiring and sustaining OEM non-core products through their remaining lifecycle.

about:
Based in Mesa, Arizona, Inter-Coastal Electronics (ICE) has spent three decades developing embedded training systems for military aviation. The company holds the Tactical Engagement Simulation System (TESS) program of record for U.S. Army aviation, delivering solutions that integrate directly with Army training ranges and Combat Training Centers. Current president David Weston joined in 2011 after engineering roles in semiconductors and aerospace, and leads a leadership team that includes veterans of Army aviation and defense acquisition.

ICE designs, develops, manufactures, tests, and supports live training hardware and software. Its core products include TESS kits for the AH-64 Apache, the TOW Improved Target Acquisition System Laser Integrated Field Training System (LIFTS), and the Training Aircraft Survivability Equipment Stimulation Suite (TASS). The company handles ruggedized electronics design, environmental and electromagnetic qualification, production transition, and depot-level repair. Recent production runs include 12 TESS kits with ground support for Morocco, and maintenance contracts spanning Fort Cavazos, Texas, and multinational sites in the United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, and Qatar.

The U.S. Army’s Program Executive Office for Simulation, Training and Instrumentation (PEO STRI) and Combat Training Centers at the National Training Center, Joint Readiness Training Center, and Joint Multinational Readiness Center use ICE systems.

ICE emphasizes a Modular Open Systems Architecture (MOSA) approach to ensure interoperability and reduce lifecycle cost. The company cites its 30-year domain experience, low-risk acquisition profile, and immediate range interoperability as key differentiators.

The company produces a comprehensive range of wire products including bare copper wire, tinned copper wire, tinned copper tubular and flat braids, and stainless steel tubular braids. Its capabilities span wire drawing, conductor fabrication, and custom wire solutions, with single-end wires available from 44 AWG to 2 AWG, stranded wires for electronics and cable assemblies, and braided wires for RFI/EMI shielding. The firm notes it offers thousands of products and serves customers across the United States and Europe.

International Wire serves markets including advanced manufacturing and automation, electrification and power infrastructure, aerospace and defense systems, data centers and critical connectivity, transportation and e-mobility, smart living and appliances, energy extraction and processing, healthcare and medical devices, and built environment and infrastructure. Specific applications cited range from robotics and factory automation to solar farms, wind turbines, nuclear energy, in-flight entertainment and cabin management systems, 5G networks, electric vehicles, home appliances, oil and gas operations, medical devices, and building wiring and grounding.

The company states its mission is to deliver value-driven, high-quality wire products and services that exceed client expectations, guided by core values of safety, people, customers, products and services, conduct, and continuous improvement. It emphasizes decades of experience in wire drawing, conductor fabrication, and custom wire solutions as a foundation for its offerings.
